doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: New York sessions, studio work and Midnight Blue
title: Looking through the Lord discography
summary: Brown reads the session count, early Detroit sessions and New York dates; Burrell wants an updated discography.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, according to the Lord’s discography you have no less than approximately 600 entries, that means you were on 600 different recording sessions.
Wow, I didn’t realize it was that many.
Over 128 as a leader.
I thought it was about a 103, it’s a hundred, I better get that…
Well, there are some sessions that he’s got in here that are from Detroit prior to the Dizzy.
Right.
So, there are some of those, maybe that’s what kind of…
Yeah, a couple of those, just a couple though.
Here’s one with Kenny Burrell and the Four Sharps.
Yeah, how can I get a copy of that?
Uh, probably I don’t know, but I’ll look tonight, I’ll go up and Google and see if it’s available.

I appreciate it, here’s the reason, because they’re doing part of my, they have a five-year review here every now and then, and part of my review is they want a discography updated, and I don’t have an updated discography.
This is the Lord’s, this is available on CD, so this is from, I only got the 2007, so it’s current now…
Is that 2007?
This is 2007, so there’s a 2009 that is going to be even more updated than this.
Okay, I can’t download that, can I? I have to buy it?
You probably have to buy it, you probably, I probably can loan this to you, we’ll work it out.
Okay, okay, I appreciate it, yeah, I appreciate it.
But, you know, and here’s a session from Detroit 1952-53 Joe Alexander, Otis “Boo Boo” Turner, Ali Jackson, Oliver Jackson…
That’s who I was thinking about, Oliver Jackson. Brown:…and “Boo Boo” Turner, Clarence Gene Shaw on trumpet, and so yeah, these are from ’53, ’52.
Yeah, I was thinking about Oliver Jackson before, I couldn’t think of his name, we went to Mille High School.
The next one is Ray Bryant with George Duvivier and Art Taylor, that’s…
That’s New York, I’m sure…
Yeah, that’s when you get to New York, so that’s the beginning of the New York sessions. So then Frank Foster and Frank Wess.
I didn’t do all that.

Then Kenny Burrell, and then Kenny Burrell March 12, 1956. And this is the session that they actually cribbed from this to actually put things like in you, in The Best of Kenny Burrell. So these are sessions before you were actually able to do your Introducing Kenny Burrell.
Well, there was a, yeah, right, well anyway, I would like to get a hold of that because I got to turn that in soon.
Okay, alright, like I said, we’ll work on it.
I’d appreciate it if you can help me with that.
